```{r}
# =============================================================================
# TARGETED IDW INTERPOLATION FOR LEVEE REMOVAL
# =============================================================================
# Purpose: Fill structure pixels in a DEM using IDW interpolation from 
#          donut ring reference points — WITHOUT computing IDW wall-to-wall.
#
# Inputs:
#   1. DEM raster (WorldDEM Neo, 5m)
#   2. Structure mask raster (anthroporas: 1 = structure, 0 = ground)
#   3. Donut ring points (GeoPackage with VALUE column = elevation)
#
# Output:
#   DEM_corrected.tif — the DEM with structures replaced by IDW surface
# =============================================================================

# ---- 1. Load libraries ----
library(terra)   # Modern raster handling (read, write, manipulate rasters)
library(sf)      # Read vector data (.gpkg points file)
library(RANN)    # Fast nearest-neighbor search using KD-trees


# ---- 2. Set file paths ----
dem_path    <- "H:/GIS_Structure/GE_Working_Folder/03_GE_Analysis/03b_GE_Intermediate_Files/DEM_prepatation_intermediate/WorldDEMNeo_zu_5m.tif"
mask_path   <- "H:/GIS_Structure/GE_Working_Folder/03_GE_Analysis/03b_GE_Intermediate_Files/DEM_prepatation_intermediate/Mask_Structure.tif"
points_path <- "H:/GIS_Structure/GE_Working_Folder/03_GE_Analysis/03b_GE_Intermediate_Files/DEM_prepatation_intermediate/Points_for_Interpolation.gpkg"
output_path <- "H:/GIS_Structure/GE_Working_Folder/03_GE_Analysis/03b_GE_Intermediate_Files/DEM_prepatation_intermediate/DEM_corrected.tif"
```

```{r}
# ---- 3. Load the data ----
dem <- rast(dem_path)
# rast() is terra function to read a raster file into R.
# It creates a SpatRaster object like a QGIS raster layer.

mask <- rast(mask_path)

pts <- st_read(points_path)
# st_read() from the sf package reads vector files (shapefiles, gpkg, geojson, etc.)
# It returns a "simple features" data frame, like a regular table but with a geometry column.
```

```{r}
# ---- 4. Quick sanity checks ----
# Let's make sure everything lines up before we start processing.

# Check that DEM and mask have the same dimensions and CRS
cat("\n--- Sanity Checks ---\n")
cat("DEM dimensions:", nrow(dem), "rows x", ncol(dem), "cols\n")
cat("Mask dimensions:", nrow(mask), "rows x", ncol(mask), "cols\n")
cat("DEM CRS:", crs(dem, describe = TRUE)$code, "\n")
cat("Points CRS:", st_crs(pts)$epsg, "\n")
cat("Number of donut ring points:", nrow(pts), "\n")

# Check that the VALUE column exists
if (!"VALUE" %in% names(pts)) {
  stop("ERROR: Column 'VALUE' not found in points file! Check column names with: names(pts)")
}
cat("Elevation range in points:", round(min(pts$VALUE, na.rm = TRUE), 2), 
    "to", round(max(pts$VALUE, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "m\n")
cat("--- End Checks ---\n\n")
```

```{r}
# ---- 4b. Align mask to DEM ----
# The mask is on a slightly different grid than the DEM (2m offset, different cols).
# resample() reprojects the mask onto the exact same pixel grid as the DEM.
# We use method = "near" (nearest neighbor) because the mask is binary (0/1) 
# we don't want averaging, which would create decimal values like 0.5.

mask <- resample(mask, dem, method = "near")

cat("Mask after resample:", nrow(mask), "rows x", ncol(mask), "cols\n")
cat("Extents match:", ext(dem) == ext(mask), "\n")

# Verify it's still binary (only 0 and 1)
mask_unique <- unique(values(mask))
cat("Unique mask values:", sort(mask_unique[!is.na(mask_unique)]), "\n")
```

```{r}
# ---- 5. Extract coordinates from the donut ring points ----
# We need a simple matrix of [X, Y] coordinates for the KD-treez and a vector of elevation values.

# st_coordinates() extracts X and Y from the geometry column
pts_coords <- st_coordinates(pts)  # Returns a matrix with columns X and Y
pts_z      <- pts$VALUE            # The elevation values

cat("Reference points ready:", nrow(pts_coords), "points\n")
```

```{r}
# ---- 6. Build the KD-tree on reference points ----
# A KD-tree organizes points in space so that finding nearest neighbors is very fast. Instead of measuring distance to all points (slow),it partitions space like a binary search tree and only checks nearby branches. This takes the search from O(n) to roughly O(log n).

# We build the tree once on the donut ring points, then query it for each structure pixel.
# nn2() from RANN will build the tree and search it in one call (Step 8). So we just prepare the data here.

# ---- 7. Find which pixels need filling ----
# Instead of looping over the entire DEM, we only identify pixels where the mask == 1 (structures that need replacement).

# Read the mask values into a vector
mask_values <- values(mask)  
# values() extracts all pixel values from a raster as a vector.
# Each element corresponds to one pixel, in row-major order (row 1 left to right, then row 2, etc.)

# Find the indices where mask == 1
# which() returns the positions (indices) where the condition is TRUE
fill_idx <- which(mask_values == 1)

cat("Pixels to fill:", length(fill_idx), 
    "out of", ncell(dem), "total",
    paste0("(", round(100 * length(fill_idx) / ncell(dem), 2), "%)\n"))

# Now get the X,Y coordinates of those pixels
# xyFromCell() converts cell indices to geographic coordinates
fill_xy <- xyFromCell(dem, fill_idx)
# This returns a matrix with columns x and y — the center coordinate of each pixel.
```

```{r}
# ---- 8. Run targeted IDW using KD-tree ----
# This is the core step. For ONLY the structure pixels, we:
#   1. Find the 12 nearest donut ring points (using the KD-tree)
#   2. Compute IDW weighted average of their elevations
#
# IDW formula:
#   weight_i = 1 / distance_i^power
#   z_estimated = sum(weight_i * z_i) / sum(weight_i)
#
# Parameters:
k     <- 12   # Number of nearest neighbors
power <- 2    # IDW power (higher = more local influence)

cat("Running IDW interpolation on", length(fill_idx), "pixels...\n")
cat("Parameters: k =", k, "neighbors, power =", power, "\n")

# nn2() is the most important command:
#   - First argument: the DATA points (donut ring) — it builds the KD-tree on these
#   - Second argument: the QUERY points (structure pixels) — it searches for each of these
#   - k: how many nearest neighbors to return
#
# It returns:
#   $nn.idx  — matrix of indices (which reference points are nearest)
#   $nn.dists — matrix of distances to those neighbors

t_start <- Sys.time()  # Track how long it takes

nn_result <- nn2(
  data  = pts_coords,   # Reference points (donut ring) — [X, Y] matrix
  query = fill_xy,      # Query points (structure pixels) — [X, Y] matrix
  k     = k             # Number of nearest neighbors
)

# nn_result$nn.dists is a matrix: each row = one structure pixel, 
#                                  each column = distance to the k-th nearest neighbor
# nn_result$nn.idx is a matrix:   same shape, but contains the INDEX of each neighbor
#                                  (pointing into pts_z)

# Now compute IDW weights and interpolated values
# We use vectorized operations

distances <- nn_result$nn.dists  # Matrix: [n_fill_pixels x k]
indices   <- nn_result$nn.idx    # Matrix: [n_fill_pixels x k]

# Handle edge case: if a query point is exactly on a reference point,
# distance = 0, which would cause division by zero.
# Replace zeros with a very small number.
distances[distances == 0] <- 1e-10

# Compute weights: 1 / distance^power
weights <- 1 / (distances ^ power)
# This is a matrix of the same shape as distances.
# Closer points get MUCH higher weights (because of the squaring).

# Get the elevation values of the neighbors
# indices tells us WHICH reference points are nearest, so we use it to look up z values
neighbor_z <- matrix(pts_z[indices], nrow = nrow(indices), ncol = ncol(indices))
# This creates a matrix where each row has the elevations of the 12 nearest points

# Compute weighted average for each pixel:
#   sum(weight * z) / sum(weight)
# rowSums() adds up values across columns for each row
idw_values <- rowSums(weights * neighbor_z) / rowSums(weights)

cat("IDW computation complete.\n")
cat("Interpolated elevation range:", round(min(idw_values), 2), 
    "to", round(max(idw_values), 2), "m\n\n")
```

```{r}
# ---- 9. Build the corrected DEM ----
# Start with a copy of the original DEM, then replace ONLY the structure pixels.

dem_corrected <- dem  # This creates a copy of the DEM raster

# Read the DEM values into a vector so we can modify them
dem_vals <- values(dem_corrected)

# Replace structure pixels with our IDW-interpolated values
dem_vals[fill_idx] <- idw_values

# Write the modified values back into the raster
values(dem_corrected) <- dem_vals

# ---- 10. Save the result ----
cat("Saving corrected DEM to:", output_path, "\n")

writeRaster(
  dem_corrected, 
  output_path, 
  overwrite = TRUE,
  datatype = "FLT4S"    # 32-bit float — appropriate for elevation data
)

cat("Output saved to:", output_path, "\n")
```
